33.01-03.additionalInfo: The points innervate the lungs and the six Fu organs. Master Tung's acupuncture points, with the reaction area of the six Fu organs, address excess conditions. In this case, it concerns excess in the lower burner. The lung qi descends to the lower burner to relieve stagnation. The three points are usually needled together. These points influence the organs located in the pelvis: the rectum, uterus, and bladder. When treating hemorrhoids or anal fissures with these points, it is important to perform bloodletting of dark blood vessels in the occipital region of the leg. When needling the three points together, we also activate Li-6 Pian Li, the Luo point, and Li-7 Wen Liu, the accumulation point. The connecting and accumulation points move blood stagnation and stagnant qi, which are common causes of hemorrhoids, rectal prolapse, and irregular menstruation. Nocturnal enuresis (bedwetting) - Treatment guide: When treating bedwetting, applying moxa on GV-4 Mingmen can enhance the effectiveness of the treatment. In addition to the points listed under the indications, it may be beneficial to consider using LIJ-7 Lieque. Point Name Qi [R] - This. Mén [P f] — Gate. Jiao — Corner, horn, angle. Mén — Gate. Zhéng — Straight. The Core Concept: What is "Qi"? In this point group, the character Qi [ ] does not mean "Energy" [ l. Instead, it translates to the pronoun "Its" or "That." In classical Chinese texts, this was used as a polite euphemism for the private parts of the body—specifically, the anus, pelvic floor, and urogenital region. Therefore, these three points map out the structural anatomy of the pelvic floor: 1. Qi Men - "Its Gate." Meaning: Represents the main opening itself. Clinical Focus: Targets the anal sphincter and vaginal opening directly. It is the primary point for opening and healing the "gate" at the bottom of the torso. Mén [B] — Gate. 2. Qi Jiao - "Its corner." Meaning: Represents the margins, edges, or lateral borders of the gate. Clinical Focus: Targets peripheral issues related to the opening, such as anal fissures (tears at the edge), external hemorrhoids, and lateral pelvic inflammation (e.g., ovaritis). 3. Qi Zheng - "Its Upright / center." Meaning: Represents the central core and the mechanical action of keeping things "upright" and in their correct position. Clinical Focus: Utilizes a lifting action to treat deep, central, or collapsed conditions. It is crucial for lifting rectal prolapse, uterine prolapse, and treating internal hemorrhoids.

33.06.additionalInfo: 33.04 Huo Chuan, 33.05 Huo Ling, and 33.06 Huo Shan are usually needled together. When these three points are needled together, they are referred to as Shou San Huo [ 'A'], Three Fires of the Hand. In Tung's acupuncture, the Three Fires of the Hand are located on the Heart channel. These points open the chest, enhance blood circulation, and warm the Yang. They can also treat coldness and numbness in the hands and feet. These three points are highly effective in treating rib disorders and a sense of oppression in the Chest, even when the cause is emotional. They are also beneficial for treating middle and lower back pain and pain radiating to the anterolateral side of the shin and thigh. Liu Li mentions that bloodletting 33.05-06 Huo Ling/Shan can treat external invasion with high fever and the inability to sweat. Summary of Differences While all three points treat the Heart (Chest pain, distress), there are specific nuances: 33.04 Huo Chuan Lung & Heart Nerves Hearing issues, Back pain. 33.05 Huo Ling Heart Nerve Hand cramps, Finger numbness. 33.06 Huo Shan Heart & Kidney Nerves Lower Back Pain, Sciatica, Kidney inflammation, Neurasthenia. 33.07.additionalInfo: 33.07 Huo Fu Hai innervates the Lungs, which govern the Qi, and the Heart, which governs the Blood. Its primary action is to stimulate the Fu organs, actively encouraging them to produce and generate abundant Qi and Blood in the body. If this mechanism sounds familiar to you, it's because it functions very similarly to the classic Lower He-sea points of the Stomach, Large Intestine, and Small Intestine: Stomach 36 (Zu San Li), Stomach 37 (Shang Ju Xu), and Stomach 39 (Xia Ju Xu). In Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), these points strengthen the Blood by improving the absorption of nutrients into the body through the digestive system. As we know, ST-37 and ST-39 are also known as the Points of the Sea of Blood. Together, these three leg points stimulate the Fu organs to promote Qi and Blood production. The mechanism of action of 33.07 Huo Fu Hai on the arm is practically the same. But here is what makes Huo Fu Hai truly stand out. This is a deep tonifying point known to extend life, specifically when we apply moxibustion. In the Daoist tradition, there is a profound emphasis on strengthening the Yang to nourish life and vitality. By doing moxa on Huo Fu Hai, we directly strengthen the body's fire and Yang. In fact, pay attention to this detail: this is the only point in Master Tung•s entire acupuncture system where moxibustion is applied. Clinically, because of this incredible ability to tonify Qi and Blood and strengthen the Yang, this point is extremely important for strengthening the immune system. This also makes it highly effective for treating and rebuilding patients suffering from post-viral syndrome. It is also highly effective for respiratory issues. If you are treating a cough, you will want to use this specific combination: needle Large Intestine 11 (Qu Chi), 33.07 Huo Fu Hai, and the extra point Ding Ke. Finally, let's look at the holographic imaging. Why does it work so well for the respiratory tract? According to Master Tung's imaging principles, the area just above and below the elbow directly mirrors and treats disorders of the throat and the upper respiratory system. Point Name Huö - Fire. Fü — The hollow organs. Håi - Sea. Huö ['k] — Fire. The character "fire" in the point's name suggests its ability to strengthen Yang and warm the organs. The characters "sea" and "hollow organs" indicate its influence on the Fu organs, particularly in generating qi and blood.

33.08-09.additionalInfo: 33.08-09 Shou Wu/Qian Jin points are needled together using the Dao Ma technique. These two points open the channels and stimulate blood circulation. They innervate the lungs and liver, regulate qi, and control the movement axis from top to bottom and east to west. Therefore, 33.08-09 Shou Wu/Qian Jin are essential for treating qi and blood stagnation. When using these points for numbness, they are combined with 22.10 Shou Jie. Due to their connection to the lungs and liver, they are crucial for treating skin diseases. Their influence on the liver makes them very important for treating body toxicity, in combination with 88.12-14 Shang San Huang and DT.01-02 Fen Zhi Shang/Xia. Bloodletting can be performed on the occipital area and the anterior side of the leg to enhance the detoxifying ability of 33.08-09 Shou Wu/Qian Jin. Because of their liver connection, these points can also treat high cholesterol. Two of Tung's 72 Absolute points and two of the 32 Solution points. Master Tung used these points to treat numbness and toxicity (drugs, food, alcohol, insect bites) together with Shou Jie 22.10. Liao Li These points strengthen metal to control wood, as indicated by their name. Therefore, they primarily treat liver diseases, especially when there is blood toxicity. Imaging Imaging between the upper and lower limbs: The area of the points mirrors the calf; hence, these points can treat calf swelling and sciatica. Point Name Shöu [+] — Hand. Wü - Five. Shöu [3] — Hand. Qiän [+] — Thousand. Jin - Metal. There are three groups of points with the name Thousand/Five Metal: 11.08 Zhi Wu Qian Jin: Finger Five and Finger Thousand Metals. 33.08-09 Shou Qian/Wu Jin: Hand Thousand/Five Metal. 77.24-25 Zu Qian/Wu Jin: Foot Thousand/Five Metal. Wü [E] - Five. Jin [ft] — Metal. The character "hand" in the point's name indicates that the points are located on the hand. The numbers five and ten in the Yellow River chart represent the earth's phase. In the nurturing cycle, the earth nourishes metal. A thousand is a multiple of ten, which links the point to the earth phase. The character "metal" in the points' names suggests their mechanism of action: nourishing metal to control wood. The connection to the earth in the points' names also implies the effect these points have on the four limbs associated with the earth.

33.15.additionalInfo: It is common practice to needle 33.13 Ren Shi, 33.14 Di Shi, and 33.15 Tian Shi together using the Dao Ma technique. This combination is known as the Three Scholars (San Shi [E±]). This combination can treat conditions affecting the lungs, heart, lower back, and upper and lower limbs. The three points have a special effect for treating asthma. The Three Scholars also impact the kidneys: 33.13 Ren Shi treats proteinuria, while 33.14 Di Shi and 33.15 Tian Shi address kidney deficiency. The lungs can strengthen the kidney Qi. The Qi of the lungs descends to stimulate the kidney Qi, and metal (lungs) nourishes water (kidneys) according to the generating cycle of the Five Phases. Master Tung For the treatment of asthma, the Three Scholars are needled on both sides in combination with 22.05 Ling Gu.
